fields.label: Name
fields.description: What the crew calls it — “north basin pump vault”. The name on the radio, not a code.

fields.label: Feature
fields.description: The fountain or feature it serves, when it is one of ours.

fields.label: Classification
fields.options:
Permit-required
Non-permit confined space
Not a confined space
fields.description: Default is PERMIT-REQUIRED, and that default is the safe direction: a space wrongly classified as needing a permit costs twenty minutes, and one wrongly classified as not needing one is how people die in pits. Downgrading is a decision somebody makes and signs for.

fields.label: Classification reviewed
fields.description: A space changes. New chemical dosing, a failed vent, standing water that was not there last year.

fields.label: Why it is one
fields.description: The four tests. A space is permit-required if it has ANY of them.

fields.label: Hazardous atmosphere
fields.description: Oxygen deficiency from decomposition or displacement, chlorine or other dosing chemicals, engine exhaust. The usual one in a fountain pit, and the one you cannot see.

fields.label: Engulfment risk
fields.description: Water that can rise, or loose material that can bury.

fields.label: How you get in
fields.description: Hatch size, ladder, how far down. What the rescue team would need to know before they arrive.

fields.label: What has to be isolated
fields.description: Pumps, valves, chemical feed, electrical. Cross-check against the lockout procedure for this feature.

fields.label: Rescue plan
fields.description: “Call 911” is not a rescue plan — most confined-space deaths are would-be rescuers. Say who retrieves, with what, from outside.
